comment: One row for each rule of the universe function `regrow` (D12.2) outside the runtime, whose rows
tools/mutations/rt_fort.json holds. The rows cover the checker (check_regrow in
src/fort/check.ft), the lowering (lower_regrow in src/fort/fir_lower.ft), the rules V4 and V6 of
the rvalue `regrow` (src/fort/fir_verify.ft and rvalue_owns in src/fort/fir.ft), the translation
(regrow_value in src/fort/fir_llvm.ft), the reference interpreter (regrow_from, regrow_back and
move_owners in src/fort/fir/interpreter.ft), and the prover. The prover has no line that names
`regrow`: it reads the `move` of the operand in gen_reads, with the kill at a vacate
(kill_past), and a store of a value that is not zero in apply_store, and apply_call reads a
`call` only. Each row D12.2-prove-* adds a wrong reading of `regrow` to one of these three, and
owner/prover_regrow_test.ft or owner/prover_vacate_test.ft catches it. The rows of the kill at a vacate
are in tools/mutations/emptiness.json. The rows D12.2-run-order-* hold the place of the operand
test of the run, after the three tests of the count (passes_count_tests). The rows D12.2-words-*
hold fir.owner_word_count and fir.owner_word_at, the offsets that the runtime and the
interpreter zero, and the private constant `@.words.N` that holds them (gen.gen_words_ref,
gen_data.emit_data). D19.5-llvm-words-site holds that each site has its own constant: the
counter joins no two constants by content. D12.2-pass-pure holds that no pass removes a `regrow` (fir_passes.pure):
rule V6 gives each `regrow` a `move` operand, which fir_passes.dead keeps, so only the direct
test of the kind in fir_passes_test.ft catches the row. The rows D12.2-print-* and D12.2-parse-*
hold the text of the rvalue. D19.6-row-seventh holds the seventh parameter of a row of
runtime_sig, which only `regrow` has. The first stage runs the module suites, which compile the
mutated sources themselves. The second stage runs each program of test/lang whose name holds
`regrow`. The third stage runs each text of test/fir whose name holds `regrow`. The table runs
in the VM with the default runner after `tools/vm configure` and `tools/vm build`. The md5 guard
reads the product compiler that the build links.
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/check.ft src/fort/fir.ft src/fort/fir_lower.ft src/fort/fir_verify.ft src/fort/fir_llvm.ft src/fort/fir/interpreter.ft src/fort/owner/prover.ft src/fort/fir_passes.ft src/fort/fir_print.ft src/fort/fir_parse.ft src/fort/runtime_sig.ft src/fort/gen.ft src/fort/gen_data.ft && ninja -C build/Linux/debug fort
